title: Bidding & Cost Controls
objectives: Differentiate Lowest Cost (Highest Volume), Cost Cap, and Bid Cap bidding
Understand how bidding strategy protects profit margins when scaling
Diagnose why an ad set with a Cost Cap might stop spending

blocks.text: Bidding controls how aggressively Meta enters ad auctions on your behalf. Let's make sure you never overpay!

left.title: Lowest Cost (Highest Volume)
points: Gets maximum results at current market auction prices

right.title: Cost Cap Bidding
points: You set an average target cost ceiling (e.g. ₹120 CPL)
Meta only bids when it predicts it can meet your cap
May underspend if your cap is unrealistically low

blocks.title: The Fruit Market Analogy
blocks.text: Lowest Cost says: 'Here is ₹500, buy as many apples as possible today, whatever the market rate is.' Cost Cap says: 'Only buy apples if they cost ₹20 or less on average. If prices are high today, keep my money in my pocket!'

blocks.title: When to Use Which Strategy
items: 1. Creative Testing & New Campaigns: Lowest Cost (ensures fast data)
2. Mature Scaling with Strict Margins: Cost Cap (protects profitability)
3. Flash Sales & Time-Sensitive Events: Bid Cap (forces aggressive auction wins)

blocks.text: If you set a Cost Cap of ₹30 when the industry average is ₹120, Meta will fail to win any auctions, and your campaign will spend ₹0!

quiz.q: What happens if you set a Cost Cap that is significantly lower than current auction market prices?
options: Meta automatically gives you cheaper leads
The ad set will fail to spend budget and will stop delivering impressions
Meta charges your bank account extra penalty fees
quiz.explain: Because the algorithm is forbidden from bidding above your cap, it will lose auctions and your budget will sit unspent.

quiz.q: Which bidding strategy is recommended when testing fresh creative hooks in a brand new ad set?
quiz.explain: Lowest Cost ensures complete, consistent delivery so you gather unbiased performance data across variants.

quiz.q: What is the primary commercial benefit of using Cost Cap bidding when scaling budgets?
options: It protects profit margins by refusing to buy leads or sales that exceed your target cost ceiling
quiz.explain: Cost Cap prevents runaway acquisition costs, ensuring scale only happens at profitable unit economics.

quiz.q: True or False: Bid Cap sets a ceiling on the average cost per lead over 7 days.
quiz.explain: False! Cost Cap controls the average cost; Bid Cap sets an absolute limit on every single auction bid.

recap: Lowest Cost spends full budget for maximum volume; Cost Cap enforces an average cost ceiling.
Use Lowest Cost for testing and Cost Cap for margin protection during aggressive scaling.
